property.name: Villa San Bernardino
property.heroHeadline: A house on Lake Ypacaraí, where nothing is ever rushed.
property.tagline: Not a house for everyone. For those who understand that real luxury is space, silence, and time returned to you.
property.footerDesc: Private micro-sites for exceptional properties. Presented by appointment, never listed on portals.

paragraphs: In San Bernardino, lakefront homes are rarely listed — they pass quietly between those who already belong.
Eight hundred square metres built across 3,900 of private grounds, steps from the water and under an hour from Asunción. A residence conceived to be lived in year-round, not visited in summer.

story.title: What it feels like to arrive
paragraphs: There is a precise moment, just past the gate, when the noise of the world drops away. The drive opens, the trees close behind you, and all that remains is the lake glinting between the trunks. That feeling — of having arrived somewhere few people know — is the first thing this house offers, before you have even stepped inside.

Indoors, the architecture does not set out to impress. It sets out to accompany. Rooms that breathe, light that shifts through the day, and an infinity pool that dissolves the edge between terrace and water. Everything is arranged so that life happens without effort: a dinner that runs long, a morning with nothing in it, an afternoon with nowhere to be.

Eight hundred square metres that read less as a large house than as private territory. Six bedrooms, a gym, and 3,900 square metres of grounds: room for every member of the family to have their own, and to receive guests without anyone feeling like a visitor. Built to last, maintained to hand over today.

lifestyle.intro: Forty-eight kilometres from Asunción, San Bernardino has long since evolved beyond its origins as a summer destination. Today, it is home to a select group of families who choose to live here year-round.
introParagraphs: Forty-eight kilometres from Asunción, San Bernardino has long since evolved beyond its origins as a summer destination. Today, it is home to a select group of families who choose to live here year-round: close to the capital when needed, and removed from it when not.

The setting combines privacy, mature greenery and convenient access to the town's amenities. It is a residential enclave for those who value quiet without withdrawing from community life or the pleasures of Lake Ypacaraí.
From this privileged position, the lake can be enjoyed with a greater sense of privacy—through spaces shaped by light, rest and the outdoors.

unDiaEnCasa.titulo: Waking to light off the lake
unDiaEnCasa.desc: Light filters through the trees. Coffee on the terrace, unhurried, Ypacaraí in front of you. No traffic, only birds.
Stable connection, a quiet study looking onto the garden. Video calls with green behind you instead of a white wall.
The grill is lit, the pool is set to 28°C, and conversation unfolds without reference to the clock. Here time is not watched, it is inhabited.

unDiaEnCasa.titulo: An active pause, with a view
unDiaEnCasa.desc: Private gym with natural light over the garden. Training does not interrupt the day, it completes it. No schedules, no compromises, and no shared facilities.
A three-minute drive to the San Bernardino Yacht Club. The sun drops onto the water and the day closes quietly. Sailing, should the mood take you.
Open gourmet kitchen, living room extending onto the terrace. Comfortably seats ten, while ensuring every guest feels at home. The house receives; it never feels full.

inversion.titulo: A retreat that holds its value when everything else moves
inversion.descripcion: San Bernardino is one of the few areas in Paraguay that has neither been overdeveloped nor lost its character. Lakefront supply is structurally limited, and demand for private residential land continues to grow.

datos.label: Character of the area
datos.tendencia: No over-development, no loss of identity

plusvalia.descripcion: The structural scarcity of lakefront land and the preserved character of the area are factors that have historically supported the long-term appeal of assets of this kind. Specific projections should be assessed through a current market report.

faq.pregunta: Can viewings be arranged from abroad?
faq.respuesta: Yes. Each viewing is prepared with a video call beforehand so that the essentials are covered before you travel, and the visit itself is accompanied throughout. Advisory services are available in English, Spanish and German.

faq.pregunta: Can a foreign buyer purchase without residency?
faq.respuesta: Yes. Paraguayan law allows foreign individuals and companies to acquire urban property in full freehold, with no residency requirement and no restriction on repatriating proceeds on resale. Independent legal and tax advice is arranged as part of the process.

Partly, and it is negotiable. The kitchen is handed over fully fitted. Some of the living, dining and suite furniture can be included by agreement; the technical specification sets out exactly what is and is not included.

faq.pregunta: What does the purchase process involve?
faq.respuesta: Five stages: profile validation, private viewing, a 10% reservation deposit under private contract, legal due diligence and title verification, and execution of the public deed. The advisor coordinates with the legal and tax professionals at each stage.

faq.pregunta: What condition is it in, and when is it available?
faq.respuesta: Available immediately. The residence is owner-occupied and meticulously maintained: no outstanding works, no waiting. Handed over following a deep clean and full preparation of garden and pool.

faq.pregunta: What are the real monthly running costs?
faq.respuesta: Community charges, garden and pool maintenance, and electricity. The breakdown is set out in the running costs section. Municipal taxes are paid and up to date.
